I don't know how this could have ended up any other way. Here's my question: why was this such a trainwreck? Visceral doesn't have the best track record but they're a competent developer, for the most part. And yet Hardline is a confused jumble of mechanics and themes. What happened here?

Usually the answer is "the suits". Video gaming is big money these days and there's a lot of pressure from the investors to get something out as soon as possible and then patch it in paid dlc later. Modern graphically intensive games like BF are quite expensive to develop and studios can go under if they don't put something out after they've invested a shitload in it. Sadly this has tended towards more shit games, rather than shorter/less beautiful good games.

IMO Battlefield gained it's most popularity with BF2 and had several good games after that, with Bad Company 2 leading the way. I never picked up BF3 or BF4 with all of the talk of bugs and glitches, and then Hardline just seemed like a Payday rip off.

I wish they would go back to something simpler, without giving up the mechanics they've built with newer games.
I judge all Battlefields by the BirgirPall videos, so you never know, this one could turn out good.

Hardline is just the latest symptom of the EA infection of DICE. A good developer acquired by EA always releases progressively shittier games until it eventually enters a death spiral and folds under financial pressure. Just look at Maxis, Westwood, and Bioware if you want additional examples.
